When that heading is absent it **appends** a new section at the end of the file."

workarounds: Executor translated the entity/relationship description into a pre-rendered mermaid `code` body inside input.json because mermaid_gen.ts does not parse an abstract DSL — it formats a pre-rendered body (per AGENT.md / mermaid_gen.ts). Worth noting as a usability gap: agents handing the mermaid agent structured entity data must themselves render the Mermaid syntax.

suggestions.assertion: Preserves existing non-Mermaid page content outside the managed markers
suggestions.reason: The assertion's wording implies the agent injects *between* `<!-- wiki-mermaid: start/end -->` managed markers, but the agent actually appends a `## Diagrams` section at EOF and leaves the `wiki-mermaid: start/end` markers (with literal `(empty)` inside) untouched. Preservation passes byte-for-byte, but the 'managed markers' contract suggested by the assertion is not actually implemented. Either (a) update the assertion to reflect the real contract ('appends a `## Diagrams` section after existing content without modifying preceding bytes'), or (b) if the marker contract is desired, add a failing assertion that checks the mermaid block is injected *between* the `wiki-mermaid: start/end` markers so the gap is surfaced instead of hidden.

No assertion verifies entity content correctness — a mermaid block containing only `erDiagram\n  A ||--o{ B : x` with no attributes would pass all four current assertions. Consider adding a check that User/Order/Product entities each appear with their expected PK/FK fields (e.g., `Order { int id PK int user_id FK decimal total }`).

The many-to-many edge `Order }o--o{ Product : contains` is emitted but unchecked. If the skill only needs to support one-to-many, this is fine; if many-to-many is also in scope, add an assertion. Otherwise consider dropping it from input.json to keep the eval scope focused.

eval_feedback.overall: All four assertions pass on substantive evidence, but assertion 2 is misleading about the agent's actual marker/append contract. Recommend tightening assertion wording and adding a content-correctness check so the eval would fail on a hallucinated-but-syntactically-valid diagram.
